Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 83, verses 1–3:

﴿Woe to those who give less (than due)﴾. Al-tatfif (the giving of short measure) in the language means al-bakhs (diminishing, depriving) and al-naqs (reduction). Al-Zamakhshari explained it thus and Ibn 'Atiyya chose this meaning. It was also said that it is exceeding the limit, whether by an increase or a decrease, and Ibn al-Faras chose this meaning. This is the more apparent, because what is meant here is diminishing people's rights in measure and weight, by a person taking more than his due or reducing what belongs to another. The occasion of the revelation of the surah was that in Madina there was a man called Abu Juhayna who had two measures: he took by the fuller and gave by the smaller. According to this, the surah is Madani. It was also said that it is Makki, because it mentions the fables of the ancients, and it was also said that part of it was revealed in Makka. The command concerning short measure was revealed in Madina, since they were the people most corrupt in this matter, so God reformed them through this surah.

﴿Those who, when they take a measure from people, take it in full﴾. The meaning of "when they take a measure from people" is that they receive from them by measure, so 'ala (on) has the sense of min (from). It was substituted with min because the speech includes the sense of imposing upon them. It is permissible for "on the people" to be connected to "take in full," and the object was placed first to convey restriction (exclusivity).

﴿And when they measure or weigh for them, they cause loss﴾. The meaning of "yukhsirun" (they cause loss) is that they diminish people's rights, and it derives from khasara (loss). One says: "khasara al-rajul" and "akhsarahu ghayruhu" when he makes him suffer loss. "Kalu-hum" means: they measured for them. "Aw wazanu-hum" means: they weighed for them. Then the preposition was deleted, so the object became accusative, because each of these two verbs is transitive sometimes by itself and sometimes by a preposition. One says: "kiltuka" and "kiltu laka," "wazantuka" and "wazantu laka," with the same meaning. The second object, which is the measured or weighed item, was deleted; the wāw, which is the pronoun of the subject, refers to the defrauders, and the hā' (of "hum"), which is the pronoun of the object, refers to the people. So the meaning is: when they measure or weigh for them food or other things that are measured or weighed, they deprive them of their rights. It was also said that "hum" in "kalu-hum aw wazanu-hum" is an emphasis of the subject pronoun. It is narrated from Hamza that he would pause on "kalu" and "wazanu" and then begin with "hum" to clarify this meaning, but this is weak for two reasons. The first is that no alif after the wāw in "kalu" and "wazanu" is established in the Mushaf, which indicates that "hum" is the object pronoun. The second is that the meaning according to this view would be that the defrauders, when they themselves undertake the measuring or weighing, diminish, and this is not the intended meaning, because the speech concerns the act and not the one who directly performs it. Do you not see that "iktalu 'ala al-nas" means: they received from them, and "kalu-hum aw wazanu-hum" means: they gave to them. So the receiving is contrasted with the giving. As for this weak view, it is a departure from the intended meaning. Ibn 'Atiyya said: the apparent meaning of the verse is that measuring and weighing are the duty of the sellers, and this is not clear. He said: the beginning of the verse concerns the buyers, who are those who demand full measure or dispute and seek more; and His saying "and when they measure or weigh for them" concerns the sellers, who are those who cause the buyer loss.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 83, verses 4–6:

﴿Do they not think that they will be resurrected, for a tremendous Day?﴾ That is, the Day of Resurrection. This is a warning to those who give less (al-Mutaffifin) and a denunciation of their deed. ʿAbdullah ibn ʿUmar, whenever he passed by a seller, would say to him: "Fear Allah and give full measure, for those who give less will be made to stand on the Day of Resurrection before the majesty of the Most Merciful." ﴿The Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds.﴾ The adverb of time (al-zarf) is in the accusative, governed by the word "resurrected" (mabʿuthun). It has also been said that it is governed by a hidden verb, or that it is a substitute (badal) for "a tremendous Day." The standing of people on the Day of Resurrection varies according to their states: some of them will stand for fifty thousand years, and less than that, to the extent that the believer stands for the duration of an obligatory prayer.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 83, verses 7–10:

﴿Kallā﴾ is a rebuke against cheating (al-taṭfīf) or an opening of speech. ﴿Indeed, the record of the wicked is in Sijjīn﴾. The record of the wicked (kitāb al-fujjār) is what is written of their deeds. Here "the wicked" (al-fujjār) may mean the disbelievers, or the cheaters (al-muṭaffifīn) even if they are Muslims, and the first is more apparent given His saying after this: ﴿Woe on that day to the deniers﴾. Sijjīn is a proper noun (ism ʿalam) transferred from an adjective on the pattern faʿīl for emphasis (lil-mubālaghah). Its matter has been magnified by His saying: ﴿And what will make you know what Sijjīn is?﴾ Then He explained it as: ﴿a written record﴾, meaning inscribed (maswṭūr), between the two books. It is a comprehensive book in which the deeds of the devils and the disbelievers are written. And "fujjār," which is derived from sijn in the sense of confinement (al-ḥabs), because it is the cause of confinement and constriction, in Hell, and because it is in a place of humiliation and punishment like a prison. It has been related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that it is in the lowest earth, and it has been related from him that it is in a well there. Kaʿb related from the Torah that it is in a black tree there. Ibn ʿAṭiyyah said: It is possible that the meaning of the verse is that the number of the wicked is in Sijjīn, i.e., they were recorded there in eternity (fi al-azal).

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 83, verses 13–15:

﴿The tales of the ancients﴾. It has been mentioned that ﴿Nay, but what they have earned has become a rust (ran) upon their hearts﴾. That is, what they had earned of sins covered their hearts, so it obliterated their insight and they came to be unable to distinguish right guidance from error. In a hadith: "When the servant commits a sin, a black spot is placed in his heart. If he commits another sin, the blackness increases, and it continues thus until it covers the heart, and this is the ran (rust)."

﴿Indeed, they will be veiled﴾. The disbelievers are veiled from God, which implies that the believers are not veiled. Malik and al-Shafi'i (may God have mercy on them) used this verse as evidence for the validity of the believer's seeing God in the Hereafter. The Mu'tazila (the rationalist school) interpreted it to mean that they are veiled from His mercy.

Nay, indeed the record of the righteous is in ʿIlliyyun (the highest levels).

ʿIlliyyun is a proper name for the register in which the good deeds are written. It is a plural form derived from the adjective ʿaliyy, in the pattern faʿīl for intensification. Allah magnified it by saying: ﴿And what will make you know what ʿIlliyyun is?﴾ Then He explained it by saying: ﴿It is a register inscribed.﴾ It is derived from ʿuluww (elevation), because it is the cause of the raising of ranks in Paradise, or because it is elevated in a lofty place. It has been narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that it is beneath the Throne. Ibn ʿAbbas said: it is Paradise.

"Kitābun marqūm" is in the nominative in both places, as the predicate of an omitted subject, its estimated form being "huwa kitābun" (it is a register). Ibn ʿAtiyya said: "Kitābun marqūm" is the predicate of inna, and the adverbial phrase is cancelled. This is a strained reading by which the meaning is corrupted. It has been reported in a narration what has been reported in the verse, namely that the angels ascend with a scroll containing the deeds of the servant. If Allah is pleased with it, He says: "Place it in ʿIlliyyun." If He is not pleased with it, He says: "Place it in Sijjin."

﴿Witnessed by those brought near,﴾ meaning the angels brought near (to Allah).

﴿Upon couches﴾. ﴿They gaze﴾ has already been mentioned. It is related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: they look at their enemies in the Fire. Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 83, verse 25–28:

﴿They are given to drink from a sealed wine﴾ Al-Raheeq (ar-raḥīq) is pure wine, and al-makhtum (sealed) — God explained it by saying that its seal is musk. It is also read khitamuhu (ختامه) with an alif after the taʼ, and khatimuhu (خاتمه) with an alif after the kha', with the taʼ either fatha or kasra. There are three opinions about its meaning. The first is that it derives from sealing something, in the sense of placing a stamp upon it: the meaning is that the mouth of the vessel containing it is sealed with musk, just as the mouths of worldly vessels are sealed with clay when one intends to keep and preserve them. The second is that it derives from "khatm al-shay'," meaning its completion, so the meaning is: its final portion is musk; the drinker finds at the end of his drink the scent of musk and its delight. The third is that its meaning is that its mixture (mizaj) is musk, i.e., the drink is mixed with musk; but this lies outside the derivation of the word.

﴿And for this let the competitors compete﴾ Tanafus (competition) regarding a thing is the desire for it, the eagerness to pursue it, and the crowding to obtain it.

﴿And its mixture is from Tasnim﴾ Tasnim is the name of a spring in Paradise from which the muqarrabun (those brought near) drink purely, and from which the raheeq that the abrar (the righteous) drink is mixed. This indicates that the rank of the muqarrabun is above the rank of the abrar; the muqarrabun are the foremost (al-sabiqun), and the abrar are the companions of the right (ashab al-yamin).

﴿A spring﴾ is accusative by way of praise, with a verb implied, or it is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal) from tasnim.

﴿From which drink﴾ means yashrabu-hā, the ba' being extra (zā'idah); it is also possible that it means yashrabu minhā (drink from it), or as in your saying "I drank the water with honey."

Verse 29–36 of Surah 83 (al-Mutaffifin), from Ibn Juzayy's commentary (al-Tashil):

﴿Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed.﴾ This verse was revealed concerning the chieftains of Quraysh, such as Abu Jahl and others. ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib (may Allah be pleased with him) and a group of believers passed by them, and they laughed at them and mocked them. ﴿And when they passed by them, they winked at one another﴾, meaning that some of them would signal to others, gesturing with their eyes. The pronoun in "marrū" (they passed) may refer to the believers or to the disbelievers, while the pronoun in "yataghamazūn" (they winked) refers only to the disbelievers. ﴿Jesting﴾ (fākihīn) derives from al-fukāha, which is amusement (al-lahw), meaning they took delight in mentioning the believers and in belittling them; this is what al-Zamakhsharī said. It may also mean that they were delighting in the pleasures of this world (yatafakkahūn bi-naʿīm al-dunyā). ﴿And when they saw them, they said, "Indeed, these are surely astray."﴾ That is, when the disbelievers saw the believers, they attributed misguidance to them. It was also said: when the believers saw the disbelievers, they attributed misguidance to them, but the first view is more apparent and better known. ﴿Yet they had not been sent as guardians over them﴾, meaning the disbelievers had not been sent as watchers over the believers, guarding their deeds and bearing witness to their rectitude or their misguidance. It is as if He said: their speech about the believers is idle talk on their part. ﴿So today, those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers﴾. By "today" is meant the Day of Resurrection, since it has been mentioned previously; on that day the believers will laugh at the disbelievers, just as the disbelievers laughed at them in this world. ﴿Have the disbelievers been repaid for what they used to do?﴾ The meaning of "thuwwiba" is "was recompensed"; it is said: thawwaba and athāba, meaning he rewarded him. This sentence may be connected to what precedes it, in the position of the object of "yanẓurūn" (they look), and so it is joined with what came before it; or it may be a separate question, in which case one pauses before it, and the object of "yanẓurūn" is omitted, as we mentioned concerning the "yanẓurūn" that precedes this. This latter view is more preferred because of the consistency of the two positions.

This sentence may be connected to what precedes it, in the position of the object of "yanẓurūn" (they look), and so it is joined with what came before it; or it may be a separate question, in which case one pauses before it, and the object of "yanẓurūn" is omitted, as we mentioned concerning the "yanẓurūn" that precedes this. This latter view is more preferred because of the consistency of the two positions.
